summary: The candidate correctly serializes eager per-communicator launches across streams and host threads, but is only a partial fix. CUDA graph replay bypasses the host guard, and both native implementations retain unbounded polling, so the original permanent-hang contract is not fully resolved.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before source check: the base has no SingleStreamGuard covering legacy and V2 native enqueues.
Candidate lock spans guard bookkeeping and both legacy/V2 native enqueue call sites.
Six candidate regression tests passed, including stream changes, same-stream fast path, capture bypass, lock coverage, and both communicator call sites.
On one MI355X, two host threads and two streams produced ordered numeric result 2, matching CPU reference 2. This did not execute a custom all-reduce.
Independent adversarial contract check found capture explicitly bypasses the guard and both JIT and legacy native paths retain unbounded polling; therefore full resolution is false.

gpu_execution.evidence: A real two-thread/two-stream guard-ordering probe ran on one AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950. It was not a collective, multi-GPU, CUDA, green-context, or graph-replay reproduction.

remaining_counterexamples: Two captured graphs containing all-reduces from the same communicator can be replayed concurrently on different streams; replay makes no Python guard call, and capture deliberately leaves the guard state unchanged.
The JIT custom-all-reduce polling loop remains unbounded, so a rendezvous collision or guard bypass can still hang permanently.
The legacy AOT custom-all-reduce barrier remains unbounded, so its eager host guard does not provide bounded failure for bypasses or protocol collisions.
remaining_limitations: Only one AMD MI355X gfx950 GPU was assigned; the original issue requires two NVIDIA A100 CUDA GPUs with NVLink and green contexts.
The original multi-rank CUDA deadlock and concurrent CUDA graph replay were not executable in this environment.
No native source changed in the candidate, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
No model weights, full serving path, or distributed model workload were used.
